# Story 11.1: Unit tests for a stable Electron origin across launches (red-phase)

Status: review

## Story

As a developer,
I want a red-phase unit-test scaffold asserting that the Electron main process resolves to a fixed default port — and therefore a stable `http://localhost:<port>` origin — on every launch when no override is set,
so that Story 11.2 has a defined, executable contract to make pass when it replaces the random-port resolution with a stable one.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A unit test exercises the Electron port-resolution logic (the code path at `apps/electron/src/main.ts:285-290` that currently calls `findAvailablePort()` when no override is set) and asserts the resolved port equals a single fixed default constant — not a random value. This assertion fails (red) while `findAvailablePort()` is still used for the default case.
2. A unit test invokes the port-resolution logic twice in succession with no override set and asserts both calls return the identical port, proving the origin `http://localhost:<port>` is stable across launches so cookies and localStorage persist. This assertion fails (red) while a random port is chosen each time.
3. A unit test sets `DMS_SMOKE_PORT` to a valid value in the environment, runs the resolution logic, and asserts it returns that override value — preserving existing smoke-test behavior (`parseSmokePort`, `apps/electron/src/main.ts:232`). This assertion passes today and must remain green after this story.
4. All new assertions from AC #1–#3 are written into spec files under `apps/electron` with the red-phase ones (AC #1, #2) marked `.skip()` (`it.skip`) so CI stays green while a random port is still chosen; every pre-existing Electron spec remains unskipped and green.

## Tasks / Subtasks

- [x] Task 1: Extract or expose the port-resolution logic for testability (AC: #1, #2, #3)
  - [x] 1.1 Locate the startup port resolution in `apps/electron/src/main.ts` (`main.ts:285-290`, where `findAvailablePort()` is called when no override is set). If it is inline in `app.whenReady()`, extract it into a pure, exported function (e.g. `resolveAppPort(env)` in a new or existing module under `apps/electron/src/utils/`) that takes the environment and returns the port number, so it can be unit-tested without launching Electron.
  - [x] 1.2 Keep the existing `DMS_SMOKE_PORT` override path (`parseSmokePort`, `main.ts:232`) intact inside the extracted function — the override must still win when set.
- [x] Task 2: Write red-phase unit tests for a stable default origin (AC: #1, #2)
  - [x] 2.1 Add a spec (e.g. `apps/electron/src/utils/resolve-app-port.spec.ts`) asserting the resolved port equals a fixed default constant when no override is set — mark it `.skip()` because `findAvailablePort()` still returns a random value today.
  - [x] 2.2 Add a spec asserting two consecutive resolutions with no override return the identical port (stable origin) — mark it `.skip()`.
- [x] Task 3: Write the green guard for the smoke-port override (AC: #3)

- [x] Task 4: Verify red + no regression (AC: #4)
  - [x] 4.1 Run `nx test electron`; confirm AC #1/#2 assertions are skipped, AC #3 is green, and no pre-existing Electron spec regresses or becomes skipped.

## Dev Notes

- **Root cause this Epic fixes:** `apps/electron/src/main.ts` resolves a random port on every launch via `findAvailablePort()` (`main.ts:289`) and then loads `http://localhost:${port}` (`main.ts:207`). Cookies (AD-5 auth cookie) and localStorage are scoped to the origin, so a new port each launch is a new origin — all previously-saved state is discarded. This story only writes the failing contract; Story 11.2 makes it pass.
- **Governing ADs:** AD-5 (Auth: Cognito JWT + CSRF, secure cookie) and AD-10 (Electron thin wrapper). FR-19 (Auth / session → `routes/auth/` + `plugins/`, client `auth/`).
- **Red-phase TDD convention:** this story writes failing tests marked `.skip()`; Story 11.2's FIRST task is to un-skip them, confirm red, then implement until green. Do NOT make AC #1/#2 pass in this story.
- **Testability note:** if extracting the resolution into a pure function changes `main.ts` behavior, keep the change minimal and behavior-preserving for the override path — the only intended behavioral difference (introduced by Story 11.2, not here) is that the *default* becomes fixed instead of random.
- **Testing standard:** Electron specs run under `nx test electron`. Follow existing spec conventions in `apps/electron/src/utils/*.spec.ts` (e.g. `port.spec.ts`, `health-check.spec.ts`).

### Project Structure Notes

- Modify: `apps/electron/src/main.ts` — extract the port-resolution block into an exported pure function (behavior-preserving for the override path).
- Add: `apps/electron/src/utils/resolve-app-port.spec.ts` (or extend `port.spec.ts`) with the red-phase + green-guard specs.
- No conflict: extraction is behavior-preserving; no runtime change until Story 11.2 swaps in the fixed default.
